title: Tail bound for a random Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be any set of coordinate indices, and choose a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube uniformly at random. The probability that the absolute value of its Fourier coefficient at $S$ is at least $2\sqrt n\,2^{-n/2}$ is at most $2\exp(-2n)$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is any subset of the $n$ coordinate indices
